observations: Read the request in full and looked at workflow/review/page-02.png, plus page-01.png and page-03.png for the page boundaries and assets/panels/02-3.png and 02-4.png for the art under the lettering. All were readable. The runtime gave no task identity, so task is null.

Text compared with the script and source lines 17 to 20, all exact: 02-1 caption 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.'; 02-1 label 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic'; 02-2 'We can organise our clinic workflow here.'; 02-3 'And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.'; 02-3 label 'WELBUK CARE for clinic staff'; 02-4 'One team. Better coordination.'. The two product labels are a manga addition naming the products. The source names Welbuk Practice and Welbuk Care in these panels, and page 6 has the product labels.

02-1: the white caption at top left rests on or just touches the top of Ananya's hair near the crown. It does not reach her face, gold stud, profile, the hands on the keyboard or the laptop screen. The teal label at top right covers only the window frame and wall. This is acceptable.

02-2: the tail points down-right and ends at the left edge of Ananya's head, by her hair and ear, not at her mouth. She is the only person in the panel and her lips are parted, so the speaker is clear. The balloon does not cover her face, her finger at her chin, the laptop or the notebook and pen.

02-3: the tail reaches the top of Meera's head. The protected phone in her right hand, with its calendar icon, and her face are clear. The teal WELBUK CARE label covers her lower kurta, the desk edge and the chair. In the composite, her left hand hangs just to the right of the label's right edge and stays visible. The margin is tight but nothing is cut off. The 02-3 asset confirms that the hand sits at her right-side hip beside the chair.

02-4: the balloon sits between the two women and its short tail points left to Ananya's cheek and ear. Ananya has her mouth open in mid-speech with a raised encouraging fist, while Meera smiles with her mouth closed. That acting backs up the tail, so the speaker is not ambiguous. The protected phone at Meera's side, the laptop and both faces are clear.
First-reading concern, P4 speaker clarity: resolved by the tail together with Ananya's open mouth and gesture versus Meera's closed smile.
First-reading concern, the P3 label cutting off the hand: on close inspection the hand is not covered. It is resolved, though only narrowly.
First-reading concern, the P1 caption touching the hair: it touches only the top of the hair. It is not a face, hand or prop overlap, so it is acceptable for lettering.

First-reading concern, Ananya's hair and stethoscope: in 02-4 the asset shows her hair gathered back with a looser bun mass behind the ear and face-framing strands, consistent with the front views in 01-1 and 02-2. Her face, gold stud, teal kurta and white coat match. In 02-1, the over-the-shoulder view shows no stethoscope tubing at the back of her collar. This is a minor art-continuity note for the artwork and final stages, not a lettering defect, and it does not stop her being recognised.

First-reading concern, P3 time of day and location: the 02-3 asset's window shows a purple-orange sunset sky with a dark tree, so it is evening. The interior light is cooler and whiter than the warm 02-2 and 02-4 interiors, which is why a first reader may see it as brighter. An open laptop with blank fields, a pen cup, a plant and an empty office chair beside Meera place her at a desk in the office. 02-4 then shows both women together in front of the same sunset window. This is understandable; the lighting difference is a minor art note, not a lettering problem.

My reading order without guides: the top-left caption, then the top-right teal label (same height, left to right in Western order), then the 02-2 balloon, then the 02-3 balloon at the top of the right panel, then the 02-3 teal label at the bottom of that panel, then the 02-4 balloon. Nothing was skipped.

Each text box sits clearly inside its own panel. The 02-3 label is far below the 02-3 balloon, close to the 02-4 gutter, but its teal label style ties it to the panel it covers. I did not read it as part of 02-4.
Teal labels and white narration captions look different. The teal pairs read as product name tags (Practice on the laptop, Care on the phone), not as speech.

transitions.observation: Ananya's morning resolve ('Let's make the rest simpler.') is followed by an evening office: sunset window, Ananya from behind typing into a blank setup form, and the onboarding caption. The caption and the light mark the time skip, and the laptop shows the 'simpler' plan beginning.

Same evening office and the same laptop and white coat. The camera moves from behind her shoulder to a three-quarter front view as she pauses, finger at chin, and states what Practice does. The sunset window carries over.

Ananya's 'We can organise our clinic workflow here.' is followed by Meera standing at a desk with an open laptop and an empty chair, holding up a phone. Her 'And our team...' continues Ananya's sentence. The sunset window and the office furniture place her in the same room; the cooler interior light is a minor art difference.

From Meera alone with the phone to a wide two-shot of both women in front of the sunset window. The same calendar-icon phone is now held at Meera's side and the laptop is turned toward the reader, which confirms one shared room. Ananya's closing line sums up both product beats.

From the dusk office to a bright morning reception after the page turn. Ravi, a new character, waves as he walks in through the glass door. Meera is behind the now-tidy desk with a monitor, and a navy reception phone lies on the desk. Daylight, the new arrival and the tidy desk show the time jump to the clinic running with Welbuk. There is no caption, but the page break and the change of light carry it. This answers page 2's 'What changes for patients?'

readingReview.comparison: The first reader's order matches mine and the intended order. Their open points against the current composite and assets: the P4 speaker is resolved by the tail and the speaking pose; the P3 label is close to the hand but does not cover it; the P1 caption touches only the hair crown, which is acceptable; Ananya's hair is consistent with a looser low bun seen from the front, while the stethoscope not showing in 02-1 from behind is a minor art note; the P3 time of day is evening per the sunset window, with only the interior light cooler. None of these remaining notes is a lettering defect. All balloon text, tails, reading order and protected areas pass.
